basics.name: Colin Middleton
basics.label: Lead Data Scientist
basics.summary: Lead Data Scientist with deep expertise in building prediction models and analytics capabilities that drive measurable operational efficiency and growth. Adept at establishing data science functions from the ground up, partnering with cross-functional stakeholders to align technical work with business priorities, and delivering clear, quantified results that build organizational trust in data-driven decision-making.

work.name: MedRisk
highlights: Designed and built next-generation prediction models for bill routing grounded in contract structure, delivering more granular, explainable outputs that gave business stakeholders clear visibility into routing decisions.
Architected modular codebase for model analysis pipelines, enabling flexible reuse across multiple use cases and significantly reducing the cost of future analyses.
Designed and built ETL pipeline for savings prediction models, implementing robust handling of malformed data to ensure consistent, reliable model inputs at scale.
Led cross-functional initiative to expand analytical capabilities, partnering with product and operations stakeholders to define requirements, align priorities, gather feedback, and drive adoption.
Architected intelligent backlog prioritization framework that optimized resource allocation, enabling human reviewers to focus on highest-impact work items.
Designed and built end-to-end prediction system for a bill treatment product, covering model development, scoring, and output delivery — establishing a reusable foundation for future model work.
Led effort to standardize and automate recurring analyses, reducing manual effort and enabling the team to scale output without proportional headcount growth.

work.name: Pearl Health
highlights: Led the design and implementation of a CFR-compliant forecasting framework for the Medicare Shared Savings Program client segment, resulting in 15% improved prediction accuracy, enhanced client satisfaction, and a clear business case for continued model investment.

Spearheaded development of an enterprise-grade data ingestion and versioning pipeline, enabling robust data testing, cross-version model comparison, and transparent reporting that improved trust in model outputs.
Designed and deployed a comprehensive tracking system for model inputs, producing quantified insights that directly informed sales strategy and executive decision-making.
Led 50+ individualized growth analyses for strategic prospects, directly contributing to a 30% increase in client acquisition — establishing data science as a measurable driver of revenue growth.

work.name: Pearl Health
highlights: Developed advanced forecasting and prediction models for client and prospect KPIs, leveraging statistical techniques including exponential smoothing, multivariate regression, and Theta modeling to support growth-oriented analytics for the client acquisition team.

Led the comprehensive refactoring of a mission-critical prediction tool (12k+ lines of Python), implementing modular architecture, configuration management, and documentation — transforming a fragile system into a scalable, maintainable platform for the team.
Engineered a proprietary I/O system that increased input accuracy by 25% and reduced processing time by 40%, eliminating a significant operational bottleneck and improving throughput at scale.

Conducted large-scale statistical analysis of KPI variability across provider networks, translating complex findings into operational recommendations that non-technical stakeholders could act on directly.

work.name: Gordian Data
highlights: Migrated and enhanced a client reporting tool from SAS to Python, improving maintainability and delivering a 10x reduction in runtime — a high-impact, low-disruption efficiency win.
Resolved a critical bug in a client pricing tool, increasing pricing accuracy by 5% and directly improving revenue operations.
Contributed to hiring and team-building efforts, including designing an applicant tracking system, participating in job fairs, interviewing candidates, and managing the candidate pipeline.

projects.name: Homelessness Prediction
projects.description: Collaborated with data providers and city government stakeholders to align on data strategy and present findings to the Spokane City Council.
highlights: Led training and evaluation of predictive models (Linear Regression, Cox Proportional Hazards, LSTM, Logistic Regression, ANN), achieving a peak AUC of 0.81 with Logistic Regression.
Addressed extreme class imbalance (0.39% positive class) via minority oversampling.
